findings.title: Duplicate `self.downsize` definition silently discards the 4-argument version
findings.body: `self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` is defined at line 145 and then immediately redefined at line 149 as `self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`. Ruby keeps only the last definition, so the width/height form is dead code (it also emits a "method redefined; discarding old definition" warning). Any existing caller using `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 200)` now binds `dimensions = 100` and `opts = 200`, so `opts[:force_aspect_ratio]` in `downsize_instructions` is called on an Integer and raises (`Integer#[]` with a Symbol), or silently produces the geometry `100` instead of `100x200`. The two call conventions must be merged into one method (e.g. accept either a geometry string or width/height).

findings.title: `optimize` arity change and removal of `dimensions` break external callers
findings.body: `self.optimize` was changed from `(operation, from, to, width, height, opts)` to `(operation, from, to, dimensions, opts)`, and the public helper `self.dimensions(width, height)` was deleted. Both are class methods on a model that plugins and other code can call; existing calls with five positional args will now raise `ArgumentError`, and calls to `OptimizedImage.dimensions` will raise `NoMethodError`. If the change is intended, the old signatures should be kept as thin wrappers (or all internal/plugin call sites updated).

findings.title: Downsize loop ignores conversion failures and overwrites the original file in place
findings.body: The loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)`, i.e. the ImageMagick/gifsicle input and output are the same path, and the boolean return value (false on non-zero exit or exception, see `OptimizedImage.convert_with`) is discarded. Consequences: (a) if `convert` fails part-way, the user's uploaded file is already truncated/corrupted on disk and is then stored as the upload; (b) if conversion simply fails every time, the loop spins 5 times doing nothing and the oversized file is handed to `Upload.create_for`, which rejects it with a size error the client never predicted. The loop should check the return value, break on failure, and convert into a separate temp file that replaces the original only on success.

findings.title: Animated GIFs lose animation because the animated code path can never trigger
findings.body: `OptimizedImage.optimize` selects the gifsicle (animation-preserving) instructions only when `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`. The path passed here is `tempfile.path` of a Rack multipart / download temp file, which has no `.gif` extension (e.g. `/tmp/RackMultipart2015...`), so the regex never matches and every oversized animated GIF is run through `convert input[0]`, which keeps only the first frame. Animation is silently destroyed for any GIF above `max_image_size_kb`. Additionally, gating on `SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails` is the wrong setting here: this is the original upload, not a thumbnail.

findings.title: SVG uploads are passed to `convert` and cannot be shrunk by resizing
findings.body: `FileHelper.is_image?` returns true for `.svg`, so an oversized SVG enters the downsize loop. Resizing a vector/text file by 80% does not reduce its byte size, so all 5 attempts run pointlessly, and running `convert` on it either rasterizes it or produces a file whose content no longer matches the `.svg` filename/extension stored with the upload. SVG (and other non-raster image types) should be excluded from this loop, as `OptimizedImage.create_for` already does for `.svg`.

findings.title: Up to 5 synchronous ImageMagick + ImageOptim passes per upload run in the web process
findings.body: For each oversized image the loop may invoke `convert` plus `ImageOptim.new.optimize_image!` (inside `convert_with`) five times, synchronously, on the request/`Scheduler::Defer` thread of the web process. With the upload ceiling now hard-coded at 10 MB, a single user can tie up a defer thread for many seconds of CPU-heavy work per upload, and a handful of concurrent uploads can starve that pool. This work belongs in a background job, or the number of passes should be computed from the size ratio in a single resize rather than iterating.

findings.title: Hard-coded 10 MB download cap replaces the configurable limit
findings.body: `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)` replaces `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`. Sites that configured a larger `max_image_size_kb` can no longer pull images of that size through the API URL path, and sites that deliberately set a small limit now have a 10 MB server-side download/disk/bandwidth exposure that no setting can lower. The cap should be a site setting (e.g. a new `max_upload_size_kb`) rather than a magic constant.

findings.title: Client-side size validation hard-codes 10 MB and ignores attachment/image size settings
findings.body: `maxSizeKB` was changed from `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` to a literal `10 * 1024`, so the `type` argument no longer affects the size check. Attachments are not downsized by the new server code and are still validated against `max_attachment_size_kb` in `Upload.create_for`, so a 9 MB attachment now passes client validation, is fully uploaded, and then fails server-side with an error the user was told would not happen. Sites with a `max_image_size_kb` above 10 MB are also newly blocked client-side. The limit should remain derived from the site settings (with the image case using whatever new upload ceiling the server enforces).

findings.title: 413 error message reports a hard-coded 10 MB limit
findings.body: The HTTP 413 handler now shows `max_size_kb: 10240` instead of the configured `max_image_size_kb`. A 413 comes from the web server (nginx `client_max_body_size`), which is independent of this constant, so the message will state a limit that is wrong for any deployment whose proxy limit or image setting differs from 10 MB, confusing users and support.

findings.title: No tests for the new automatic downsizing path or the changed OptimizedImage API
findings.body: The PR adds a new in-place downsizing loop in `create_upload` and changes/duplicates `OptimizedImage.downsize`/`optimize` signatures, but no specs were added or updated. A single spec for `OptimizedImage.downsize` arity would have caught the duplicate method definition, and a controller/unit spec would cover the oversized-image, conversion-failure and non-raster (SVG/GIF) cases that are currently unverified.
